- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then gradually converges or diverges later.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >40), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly — overcorrecting or plateauing.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting periods — fails to recognize when prices are drifting back toward historical averages.
- Forecast exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often takes 2–3 days to adjust downward.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility — amplifies noise in price movements, especially in the final 5–10 days of forecast.
- For long-term (30-day) forecasts, model tends to underestimate the final 5–10 days, especially when true outcomes show strong upward momentum or sudden spikes.
- Model fails to capture “rebound” or “reversal” patterns after sharp declines — often continues downward trend longer than actual.
- Model assumes linear continuation of recent trend — fails to account for structural breaks or policy-driven price shifts.
